name: Kremlin
lede: Kremlin is a deep blue-green from the Maerz and Paul dictionary of color, a name that has nothing to do with the walls it recalls.

sections.title: A dictionary name
sections.body: Our library finds Kremlin in Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary, plate 29, and the ISCC-NBS system calls the nearest block dark bluish green, 3.5 units away on the CIEDE2000 scale [1]. Why the compilers chose the word is undocumented [1].

sections.title: What the books say
sections.body: The two book hits in our collection are about the place, not the shade. Jarman describes a red flag flying high above Lenin's tomb at the Kremlin [2], and Finlay mentions a vodka brand that supplies the Kremlin [3]. Neither describes a dark teal. Anyone looking for the connection should be careful, because red is the color the books pair with the Kremlin [2], while this swatch is a blue-green close to [[teal]] and [[bottle-green]] [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, a color this close appears in 53 works, or 0.22 per cent, rarer than 58 per cent of the named colors [4]. It peaks in the 1900s, with 9 of 1,674 paintings, about 3.8 times the expected rate for the same museums [4]. These numbers are small, and they are photographs of varnished paintings, so they hint at a modern taste for dark teals without proving it [4].
